heard: There is a planet where the atmosphere is made of iron gas. 640 light years away in Pisces, gas giant WASP-B orbits its star in 1.8 days. Blasted by intense radiation, the planet has inflated to twice Jupiter's diameter. One side is trapped in eternal daylight, soaring to 2,400 degrees Celsius. That furnace rips molecules apart and boils solid iron into a gas. Ferocious winds sweep that vapor to the night side, where it cools to 1,500 degrees. Astronomers using the very large telescope tracked iron at dusk, but nothing at dawn. Researchers found that, as the night side cools, it condenses this vapor into torrential showers of liquid iron. After tracking these metallic winds, astronomers reached a surreal conclusion.
